# The Vagina Guide

> Research-backed vaginal health education by Taja, a women's health educator with 191K TikTok followers (@thevaginaguide). Topics: bacterial vaginosis (BV), yeast infections, UTIs, vaginal odor and pH, periods and PMS, and pelvic floor health. Education only, not medical advice.

## Blog articles
- [Why does BV keep coming back after antibiotics?](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/why-does-bv-keep-coming-back/): BV back again? Why more than half of women get it back within a year, the biofilm and partner reasons behind it, and what actually helps break the cycle.
- [Should your partner be treated for BV? The 2025 study that changed the conversation](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/should-my-partner-be-treated-for-bv/): A 2025 NEJM trial found treating male partners cut BV recurrence from 63% to 35%. Here's what partners took, who it applies to, and how to ask your doctor.
- [Yeast infection or BV? How to tell the difference (without guessing wrong)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/yeast-infection-vs-bv/): Itchy and cottage-cheese discharge, or thin and fishy? A side-by-side check of yeast infection vs BV, plus why most women who self-treat for yeast guess wrong.
- [Why antibiotics give you a yeast infection (and what to do next time)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/yeast-infection-after-antibiotics/): Antibiotics for a UTI or strep, then the itch starts. Why antibiotics trigger yeast infections, what the probiotic research really shows, and how to plan ahead.
- [What to eat the week before your period (to cramp less and bloat less)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/what-to-eat-before-your-period/): The pre-period plate: calcium, ginger, fiber and less salt. What the research says helps PMS, cramps and bloating in the 7 days before your period.
- [Period poops are real: why your period gives you diarrhea (and how to calm it)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/period-diarrhea/): Period poops are real and caused by prostaglandins. Why your period gives you diarrhea, how common it is, and what helps, from NSAID timing to soluble fiber.
- [How to do Kegels correctly (most women get this wrong)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/how-to-do-kegels-correctly/): Half of women do Kegels wrong after verbal instructions. How to find your pelvic floor, do the perfect Kegel, avoid the 5 big mistakes, and how many to do.
- [Why do I pee a little when I sneeze? Stress incontinence, explained](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/peeing-when-you-sneeze/): Leaking when you sneeze, laugh or jump is stress incontinence. Why it happens, the 1-second trick that helps right away, and the training that cures many women.
- [Does cranberry juice actually help UTIs? What the research really says](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/does-cranberry-juice-help-uti/): Cranberry can lower your risk of repeat UTIs, but can't cure one. What 50 trials show, why D-mannose flopped in a big 2024 trial, and what works instead.
- [UTI after sex? Why it happens and 7 ways to stop the cycle](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/how-to-prevent-uti-after-sex/): Why sex triggers UTIs, and what research says about peeing after sex, spermicide, drinking more water and a single antibiotic dose after sex.
- [Why does my vagina smell? 7 smells and what they mean](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/why-does-my-vagina-smell/): Tangy, metallic, fishy, ammonia, bready, skunky or rotten? What each vaginal smell means, which ones are normal, and when a smell needs a doctor.
- [What's a normal vaginal pH? How to test it at home (and when not to)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/normal-vaginal-ph/): Normal vaginal pH is about 3.8 to 4.5. What raises it, how to use a home pH test the right way, when results can fool you, and what a high pH might mean.
- [Vaginal discharge color chart: what clear, white, yellow, green, gray and brown mean](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/vaginal-discharge-color-chart/): Clear, white, yellow, green, gray, pink or brown? What each discharge color usually means, what's normal across your cycle, and when to see a doctor.
- [Is my discharge normal? How discharge changes through your cycle](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/discharge-during-your-cycle/): Dry, sticky, creamy, then clear and stretchy like egg white. How normal discharge changes week by week through your cycle, and which changes aren't normal.
- [15 ingredients to avoid in feminine hygiene products (and what to use instead)](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/feminine-hygiene-ingredients-to-avoid/): Fragrance, MI preservatives, talc, petroleum jelly and more. The feminine wash, wipe and lube ingredients linked to irritation and BV, plus safer swaps.
- [How to wash your vagina (actually, your vulva) the right way](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/how-to-wash-your-vagina/): Your vagina cleans itself. How to wash your vulva, whether you need soap, why douching backfires, and a simple routine for less odor and irritation.
- [11 questions to ask your gynecologist about vaginal symptoms](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/questions-to-ask-your-gynecologist/): Walk in prepared: what to do before your appointment, 11 questions that get you tested and treated properly, and what to write down before you leave.
- [How to get your doctor to take your vaginal symptoms seriously](https://thevaginaguide.com/blog/how-to-get-your-doctor-to-listen/): Told it's probably nothing, again? Scripts to ask for testing, a second opinion and a referral, plus how to track symptoms so you leave with a real plan.
